about: Per-phase roofline (src/model.js phaseBound; node report.js --roofline). Each card and CPU carries its compute ceilings by precision, its VRAM read rate and PCIe link; each engine says which precision its prefill and decode kernels run at and how its weight streams overlap the kernels; each model says its FLOPs per token by class. A phase's time is the max (engine overlap 'max', per chunk) or the sum (overlap 'sum') of its terms: compute (FLOPs / (ceiling x eta)), weight streaming (bytes not resident / link rate), resident weight reads (bytes / VRAM rate), attention and KV bytes. The bound is the time at eta 1 (the hardware ceiling); the prediction uses the engine's fitted eta (one factor per engine, fit cells named under checks). Every phase names the term that binds. build.py copies each card's and CPU's ceilings into data.boxes (gpus[].ceil, cpu.ceil) and the firmware unlock setting into gpus[].firmware_unlock.

precision_fallback.src: a setting: the ceiling a phase falls back to when the card lacks the precision its engine asks for (Turing has no BF16 tensor path, Pascal no tensor cores); the bound names the key it used. Of the chain the card has, the fastest key prices the phase (ties keep this order): the GTX 1080 Ti has FP16 at 1/64 rate, so its FP16 tensor phases run at FP32, as llama.cpp does there

shape_curves.about: Measured kernel rates of a GEMM class (experts | trunk) by kernel path and precision, as a function of rows: for experts the rows an expert sees (tokens x k / the distinct experts they touch), for the trunk the tokens in the GEMM. src/model.js shapeRate interpolates in log(rows) (power law between neighbouring points; MEASURED within 5 % of a point, ESTIMATE between and beyond, never above the square ceiling); a card, path or precision with no curve keeps the square ceiling, flagged unmeasured. bits_per_weight is the weight layout the bench read (the excess compose mode subtracts that read, see settings.shape_compose); model names the expert / trunk dims measured (another model's dims read ESTIMATE). Common bench: odie B70 #1 (0000:4c:00.0), oneDNN 3.11.4 GPU matmul (oneAPI 2026.1, ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:full-intel), Level Zero 1.15.38308, best of 5 means of 20 runs after a 3 s warm-up, the card at its 230 W limit; lab notes results-2026-11-11 (full-b70-1.jsonl, m1202-b70-1.jsonl, tbo-b70-1.txt)

shape_compose.src: a setting: how a measured shape curve (cards[].shape_curves) prices a GEMM class. excess (default): the measured kernel time less the read of its own weights at the bench layout (bits_per_weight / VRAM read), never faster than the square ceiling, because the engine's own terms already price the weights at the store's bytes (the strata pass, read.resident, read.misses, the PCIe stream) and the low-row bench points sit at the weight-read roof (int8 85 %, fp16 94 % of the VRAM read at 24 rows), so the kernel time alone would price the weights twice and at the bench layout's width. kernel: the measured kernel time as the compute term (the shape ceiling as a plain ceiling). Chosen on the held-out R8 16-agent useful rate (83.4 tok/s, not a fit cell): see docs/how-it-works.md roofline

placements.src: a setting: where a query's GEMM classes run. gpu (the default when a query or recipe states none): trunk and attention on the stage card, experts resident on it or host-side by the query's resident bytes and host path. cpu_only (a recipe's placement field, the external rows' vocabulary): trunk, attention and experts on the box CPU at its cpus ceilings x the share of physical cores the recipe's threads use, every weight read from DRAM once a chunk. A placement not in this table, or a CPU placement on a box or engine with no CPU ceiling or CPU kernel metadata, is refused (no bound), never bounded on the GPU

3090ti.src: a setting: the RTX 3090 Ti firmware unlock is on since 2026-11-10 (owner reboot); a query or recipe sets unlock stock|unlocked to judge the other state, and a check dated before since reads stock

The Q8_0 trunk runs the same int8 path (int8_cpu). Attention with -fa 1 on a CPU with no native FP16 / BF16 math (droopy has no avx512_bf16, lassie is AVX2) is taken at the FP32 rate (ESTIMATE). The convert cost and the barrier waits (ggml_barrier ~25 % of the droopy CPU-only profile, lab notes) are not separate terms: they sit in the CPU eta, fitted per engine on cells of one cpu path (cpu_fits)
